Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Reference Materials: Dictionary, Thesaurus, Encyclopaedia

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Reference Materials: Dictionary, Thesaurus, Encyclopaedia. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we use reference materials?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use the dictionary, thesaurus and subject specific encyclopaedia to check the meaning and usage of words

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 5.2.1 REFERENCE MATERIALS: DICTIONARY, THESAURUS, ENCYCLOPAEDIA
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 5.2.1 Reference Materials: Dictionary, Thesaurus, Encyclopaedia helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 5.2.1 REFERENCE MATERIALS: DICTIONARY, THESAURUS, ENCYCLOPAEDIA
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use the dictionary, thesaurus and subject specific encyclopaedia to check the meaning and usage of words

What this means
In this part you learn to use the dictionary, thesaurus and subject specific encyclopaedia to check the meaning and usage of words. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the dictionary, thesaurus and subject specific encyclopaedia to check the meaning and usage of words.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Reference Materials: Dictionary, Thesaurus, Encyclopaedia”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the dictionary, thesaurus and subject specific encyclopaedia to check the meaning and usage of words. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 5.2.1 Reference Materials: Dictionary, Thesaurus, Encyclopaedia is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Reference Materials: Dictionary, Thesaurus, Encyclopaedia”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use the dictionary, thesaurus and subject specific encyclopaedia to check the meaning and usage of words)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 5.2.1 Reference Materials: Dictionary, Thesaurus, Encyclopaedia to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use the dictionary, thesaurus and subject specific encyclopaedia to check the meaning and usage of words.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 5.2.1 Reference Materials: Dictionary, Thesaurus, Encyclopaedia from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 5.2.1 Reference Materials: Dictionary, Thesaurus, Encyclopaedia: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 5.2.1 Reference Materials: Dictionary, Thesaurus, Encyclopaedia?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we use reference materials?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 5.2.1 Reference Materials: Dictionary, Thesaurus, Encyclopaedia means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use the dictionary, thesaurus and subject specific encyclopaedia to check the meaning and usage of words.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
